signals.name: Nathan Benaich
signals.latest_title: Post on opaque maths solutions and the State of AI Report 2026 (launching Oct 8)
signals.summary: Around Sep 26-27 he argued that jumping to a maths solution in an opaque way could deprive us of knowledge humans might have discovered, and said he will cover this in the State of AI report. He also congratulated Enveda on its $311M Series E and said the report launches Oct 8.
signals.connection: The opaque-reasoning point bears on today's AI safety and governance stories, including OpenAI holding back a model and the UK AISI findings on attack behavior. The Enveda round is a sign of continued capital flowing into AI-driven science.

signals.name: Michael Burry
signals.summary: Burry said new weekend research has him moving his timelines up, and that the AI bubble may burst sooner than he first thought. He is repositioning into puts and has added shorts in Micron, Nebius, Palantir and the iShares Semiconductor ETF (per reporting on his posts).
signals.connection: He is bearish on AI while AMD is paying $8.2B for World Labs. A 10-year yield near 5.2% and oil rising on Hormuz tensions add to the pressure on richly valued AI and semiconductor names.

signals.name: Ben Thompson
signals.summary: He argues that agents are the ultimate Aggregators, which makes apps a means rather than an end, and that providing them is tech's biggest prize. His weekly roundup (Sep 25) covers the Meta vs. Amazon aggregator fight and GM giving in to CarPlay. He also interviewed Colossus EIC Jeremy Stern about profiling Zuckerberg.
signals.connection: This is the strategic frame for the AI platform race, including the AMD/World Labs deal. It also ties to the frontier labs' agent capabilities, which are the same ones behind the cyber-risk concerns at OpenAI and UK AISI.

signals.name: Packy McCormick
signals.summary: A deep dive on Airbound and humanity's flying future. His Weekly Dose of Optimism #212 (Sep 25) covered Vironexis, Solcoa, Terraform, Joby and Meta VR glasses. He also wrote on the future of education in "Would We Send Our Kids to HAA?"
signals.connection: This is an optimistic counterpoint to today's geopolitical and market stress. It matches the Applied Tech & Industry and Energy themes: hard-tech startups, aviation, and energy resilience.

signals.name: Lenny Rachitsky
signals.latest_title: How I AI: Jev for beginners + I left Claude for months, Opus 5.5 brought me back + Opus 5.5 vs. GPT-6 Sol bench
signals.summary: His weekly roundup includes a 26-minute walkthrough of Jev, which returns type-safe structured values instead of text. He calls it the fastest, cheapest classification layer he has put in a pipeline, and says he shipped three projects with it. He also has a Molly Graham episode on grief, loneliness and burnout in tech, and how delegating to AI differs from delegating to people.
signals.connection: The Opus 5.5 vs. GPT-6 Sol comparison shows the frontier-model race that OpenAI's withheld model belongs to. The Molly Graham episode connects to the Labor & Workforce theme, on AI's toll on tech workers.
